entry.summary: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area
entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Sweden's official currency is the Swedish Krona (SEK). Some businesses no longer accept cash. Declare amounts over 10,000 euros or equivalent if you're travelling between Sweden and any non-European Union (EU) country. This includes all forms of currency, not just cash. You'll be fined if you don't declare it or give the wrong information on entry or exit. You don't need to declare currency if you're travelling to or from another EU country.

laws.rule: It's illegal to use physical punishment against children, including threatening a child with physical punishment. If you use or threaten physical punishment against your child, local authorities can take custody of your child and prosecute you.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences, even for small amounts, include heavy fines and jail.

laws.rule: For specific information on bringing medication into Sweden, read the Swedish Medical Products Agency. You can bring a 3-month supply of medicine for personal use to Sweden.

tourism.detail: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.

meetings.detail: Business meetings are covered, without being employed in the country.

conference.detail: Business travel, including conferences, is covered.

unpaid-speaking.detail: Unpaid speaking during a business visit is generally covered; the paid-activity exclusion is read narrowly.
unpaid-speaking.next: If unsure, ask Embassy of Sweden, Yarralumla.

paid-speaking.detail: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Embassy of Sweden, Yarralumla.
paid-speaking.next: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Embassy of Sweden, Yarralumla.

remote-work.detail: Remote work for an employer outside the EU isn't addressed in the EU guidance read.
remote-work.next: Ask the Embassy of Sweden, Yarralumla.

entrepreneur.detail: Exploring and meeting fit a business visit; running a business needs national permission.
entrepreneur.next: Ask the Embassy of Sweden, Yarralumla.

trade.detail: Business visits are covered; selling or delivering services may be paid activity.
trade.next: Keep the trip to meetings and negotiation.

artist.detail: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Embassy of Sweden, Yarralumla.
artist.next: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Embassy of Sweden, Yarralumla.

mixed-mission.detail: The visa-free stay covers the business and tourism parts; any paid part needs national permission.
mixed-mission.next: Ask the Embassy of Sweden, Yarralumla.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of Sweden, Yarralumla about filming, and the local authority about locations.

research.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (short-term study or training)
research.detail: Short-term study and training are covered; paid research at an institution is paid activity.
research.next: Ask the Embassy of Sweden, Yarralumla if the host pays you.

volunteering.detail: Volunteering isn't addressed in the EU guidance read.
volunteering.next: Ask the Embassy of Sweden, Yarralumla.
